scenarios.name: Balanced baseline
scenarios.description: Mixed inference, embedding, evaluation, and training loads with arrivals spread through the horizon.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 60-minute primary evaluation window; the staggered arrivals and 18-minute maximum nominal duration leave substantial service margin, but the horizon is not a drain-to-empty guarantee.

scenarios.name: Burst arrivals
scenarios.description: Large batches arrive together and again later, contending for a shared queue.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 75-minute primary evaluation window preserves three burst waves and a long post-arrival service window; it measures backlog recovery without extending selectively for any policy.

scenarios.name: Mixed priorities and tight deadlines
scenarios.description: Latency-sensitive workloads share capacity with lower-priority batch work.
scenarios.intended_stress: Priority ordering versus deadline and throughput trade-offs.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 70-minute primary evaluation window spans the staggered queue and 65-minute maximum nominal deadline; it evaluates deadline outcomes rather than promising that all jobs drain.

scenarios.name: Heterogeneous GPU requirements
scenarios.description: Workloads require different accelerator classes across a mixed-capacity pool.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 65-minute primary window exceeds the staggered arrival and maximum nominal service interval; structurally incompatible GPU/memory requests remain visible as infeasible, not as horizon failures.

scenarios.name: GPU memory pressure
scenarios.description: Memory-heavy jobs compete across nodes with sharply different memory per accelerator.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 65-minute primary window provides service time beyond the 58-minute maximum nominal deadline while retaining the intentionally skewed memory topology; impossible placements are terminally diagnosed.

scenarios.name: Tight facility power budget
scenarios.description: Node power limits are compatible with the pool, but the facility budget restricts simultaneous work.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 70-minute primary window includes the 65-minute maximum nominal deadline and leaves time for post-deadline execution; facility power contention is intentionally not removed by extending the horizon.

scenarios.name: Node failure and recovery
scenarios.description: Active nodes fail stochastically; affected workloads can be requeued and retried.
scenarios.intended_stress: Failure handling, recovery, and requeue behaviour.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 90-minute fault-injection window spans the 80-minute maximum nominal deadline and permits repeated three-step recovery cycles; stochastic failures may still leave valid work unresolved.

scenarios.name: Short jobs versus long-running work
scenarios.description: Long training reservations compete with short latency-sensitive workloads arriving throughout the run.
scenarios.intended_stress: Queue delay and starvation under mixed service times.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 90-minute contention window exposes the queueing burden of three simultaneous 60-minute, four-GPU jobs on two fitting nodes; the serialized service lower bound exceeds the horizon before later short jobs are included.

scenarios.name: Infeasible workloads
scenarios.description: A mixed feasible queue includes requests exceeding all node resource envelopes.
scenarios.intended_stress: Explicit detection of impossible GPU and memory requests without unsafe placement.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 45-minute primary window is designed to evaluate the feasible portion of the mixed queue; 12-GPU/512-GB requests exceed every node envelope and are reported as permanent infeasibilities.

scenarios.name: Combined operational stress
scenarios.description: Burst arrivals, mixed priorities, GPU-type requirements, power pressure, and node failures interact.
scenarios.intended_stress: Compound constraints and policy trade-offs under shared exogenous failures.
scenarios.horizon_rationale: Fixed 90-minute compound-stress window spans the 80-minute maximum nominal deadline while keeping bursts, power limits, model constraints, and seeded failures active; it is not extended to force queue drain.
